newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt rearrests Islamists in Sadat case -group.
newsitem.headline: Egypt rearrests Islamists in Sadat case -group.

text.p: The Egyptian authorities have put back in jail 17 Islamist militants who had just completed 15 years in prison for their links with the group that assassinated president Anwar Sadat, a human rights group said on Sunday.
The group, the Committee for the Defence of Prisoners of Opinion, said in a statement that it condemned the arrests and demanded the authorities release the 17 immediately.
"It violates the most basic principles of the rule of law and human rights...Egypt cannot rise to the ranks of civilised states as long as human rights violations continue," it said.
The committee said the 17 were members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) and the Jihad Group and had been imprisoned in the Sadat assassination and Jihad cases.
It was the Jihad group which carried out the assassination of Sadat at a military parade in Cairo on October 6, 1981.
The Interior Ministry information department said it had no information on the case.
